newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank provides loan for Colombian oil project.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank provides loan for Colombian oil project.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Japan said it signed an agreement on Friday to provide an untied loan worth $300 million to Colombia's Empresa Colombian de Petroleos (ECOPETROL) to develop the nation's largest oil field.

The bank will provide 70 percent of the total, or $210 million. The remaining $90 million would be co-financed by 14 private Japanese banks, lead-managed by Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, the Export-Import Bank said in a statement.
The loan was extended in response to a request from the Colombian government in 1994. Total funds necessary for the project will amount to $4.4 billion, it said.
The field will be developed with major European and U.S. oil companies, and almost all the crude produced will be exported to Europe and the United States, the statement said.
The bank said the project is intended to increase production at the oil field from the current 170,000 barrels per day to 500,000 by the end of 1997.
